To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the peroxidase-catalase superfamily has undergone an evolution from the catalase-type to cytochrome c, ascorbate and non-heme peroxidases, with hybrid-type A and B peroxidases as the key turning points.

1) the peroxidase-catalase superfamily is composed of at least 11 families of heme peroxidase enzymes, 2) the phylogeny of the whole superfamily is complex and includes several hybrid-type peroxidases that evolved from different ancestors, and 3) the evolution of the peroxide metabolism and the peroxide signaling in the eukaryotic cell is much more complex than previously thought.
“Hybrid-type peroxidases represent new members of heme b -containing peroxidase–catalse superfamily that have evolved in parallel to other peroxidases in fungi and eukaryotic organisms.”
In summary, our research is concerned with

the reconstruction of the evolutionary history of heme peroxidase–like enzymes and their catalases and with the identification and description of new enzyme families and their evolutionary relationships.
the evolutionary history of the peroxidases, which are the most abundant and functionally diverse heme-containing enzymes.
the evolution of the heme peroxidase family in the eukaryotic domain and provides a basis for future functional studies of the peroxidases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peroxidase-catalase superfamily is a complex and dynamic enzyme superfamily, with many evolutionary events and gene duplication/loss events.
the peroxidase superfamily evolved from a single ancestral protein by a combination of gene duplication, horizontal gene transfer, domain shuffling and fusion, as well as domain loss.
the evolution of peroxide metabolism and its regulation in eukaryotic organisms has been driven by a complex network of gene fusions and gene duplications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phylogenetic reconstruction of the peroxidases–catalases superfamily based on the full-length protein sequences has revealed the existence of two new (hybrid) families of eukaryotic peroxidases.
the phylogeny of the peroxidases and their evolutionary history are more complex than previously thought.
the evolution of peroxide detoxification enzymes was a complex and long process involving multiple independent gene duplication events and subsequent gene fusions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolutionary history of the superfamily was much more complex than previously thought.
the peroxidase superfamily is much more complex and diversified than previously anticipated.
the evolution of the heme peroxidase superfamily was much more complex than it was believed before.
